fields.AN_Notes: Theoretical essay that proposes hermeneutic reverse engineering (Balsamo 2011) as a method to examine data and algorithmic bias in AI systems from an intersectional feminist standpoint. AN_Bias_Axes: race is developed as the work's own worked example in the sections on data and algorithms (face detection failing on a dark-skinned face, search results for 'three black teens'), gender through the face example ('societal definitions of race and gender') and the Keyes example on binary gender recognition; the opening list of race, gender, ability, language, class, economic background and religion is an enumeration and is not coded. Intersectional is not coded because no passage makes an outcome depend on a combination of axes, although the frame is intersectional feminism. AN_Harm_Types: Erasure from the work's own finding that questioning data reveals whose cultural narrative is missing, Exclusionary_Norms from its own conclusion that the method questions what is normal in a system and who falls outside that norm; the disparate recognition of dark-skinned faces and the misclassification cases are cited from other work and not coded. AN_Mitigation_Stage and Status: participatory design and co-design workshops plus actionable AI audits are proposed as research perspectives, nothing is demonstrated or evaluated. AN_Prompting_Role None: observing outputs for different prompts appears once as a cited interrogation idea. AN_Gender_Understanding Unclear: gender is treated through examples, the work states no own understanding of gender; the critique of binary gender recognition is cited from Keyes (2018). AN_Task None: AI is the object of critique, no professional task of AI use is described.

fields.AN_Notes: Global reference framework of twelve AI competency blocks for school students (four aspects by three progression levels) with curricular goals, pedagogical methods, learning environments and assessment items. Bias enters as the non-discrimination principle, the inclusivity principle (section 2.4), a data biases lab and the competency to critique AI-amplified biases. AN_Bias_Axes None: gender, ethnicity, culture, ability, socio-economic status and language appear only in enumerations of bias types or of disaggregation variables; no axis is analysed or developed as a worked example. AN_Harm_Types None: the framework names biases and inequality as learning topics but establishes no harm mechanism for its own object. AN_Mitigation_Stage: Pre_Processing (representative data, data engineering to remove identifiable biases in the data biases lab), In_Training (anti-discrimination training methods, discrimination-free methods for training machine learning) and Organisational_Process (rigorous public validation mechanisms before recommending AI tools, inclusive testing and auditing); all are recommended as curricular content or policy, none is demonstrated or evaluated, hence Proposed. AN_Bias_Definition Implicit_Only: bias is understood as discrimination embedded in tools and outputs and as data imbalance, without a determination. AN_Gender_Definition and Understanding Not_Applicable: gender occurs only in enumerations, the Gender category is coded nein for this reason. AN_Population Not_SW_Specific: school students in general education; Education_Professional does not apply to school settings. AN_Task None: the framework treats AI as curriculum content; the use of AI tools for assessment appears only as a supplementary outlook for school teaching. AN_Prompting_Role None: prompts appear only in a privacy assessment item.

fields.AN_Notes: Survey of bias evaluation metrics, evaluation datasets and mitigation techniques for LLMs with three taxonomies and a harm taxonomy (Table 1). AN_Harm_Types: all nine values structure the survey's own synthesis as rows of Table 1 (representational harms and allocational harms) and, for six of them, as coded columns of Table 4; the Derogatory_Language row label is lost in the conversion of Table 1, so its passage comes from section 2.4.2. AN_Bias_Axes: coded from the targeted-social-group columns of Table 4 (age, gender identity, nationality, physical appearance, race, religion, sexual orientation) and from dialect as the survey's own worked example (African-American English, linguistic profiling); disability and socioeconomic status appear only in dataset enumerations and the 'Other' footnote and are not coded. Intersectional is not coded: the survey argues that group fairness can hold for each group while failing for intersectional subgroups, but names no axis combination whose result it develops. AN_Prompting_Role Research_Instrument: prompt datasets (sentence completions, question answering) are a class of the evaluation taxonomy; modified prompting language is reviewed as a mitigation technique, not recommended. AN_Prompt_Techniques General_Guidance, concrete strategy as synthesised: 'prompting language with different levels of abstraction to instruct the model to avoid using stereotypes' and prepending positive adjectives or phrases to a prompt (section 5.1.4). AN_Mitigation_Stage: the four technical stages are the survey's own taxonomy; Prompt_Practice from modified prompting language; Organisational_Process from participatory research designs, reporting standards and data governance proposed in section 6. AN_Mitigation_Status Evaluated as a synthesised evaluation, not the survey's own experiment: the survey reports that Borchers et al. (2022) found instructions prompting diversity or gender equality unsuccessful for bias removal, and that pruning 10-20% of parameters increased resistance to jailbreaking (Hasan, Rugina and Wang 2024); other techniques are inventoried without assessment. AN_Gender_Understanding Social_Construct: the survey states that social groups, which by Definition 3 include gender identity and sex, are socially constructed, contested and tied to power imbalances, and it adopts the critique that binary and immutable gender modelling erases trans, nonbinary and intersex people; its own Figure 1 example uses a male and female substitution. AN_Gender_Definition Implicit_Only because gender itself is not defined. AN_Task None: general LLM bias survey without an application task.
